# AI Teams — Routing Index

<!-- GENERATED by ai/teams/gen-index.sh — do not edit by hand. Regenerate: bash ai/teams/gen-index.sh -->

Two-level routing: pick a **team** by domain/keywords, then a **member** by role.
Installed agents are invoked as `@agent-<team>-<role>` (Claude) / `<team>-<role>` (Gemini/Antigravity)
/ `teams-<team>-<role>` (Ollama). Run `/team <team|squad>` to surface a curated set.

## Teams

### 🎨 web — Web Development

| member | invoke | tier | use when | avoid |
|--------|--------|------|----------|-------|
| api | `web-api` | standard | Designing or changing backend HTTP/GraphQL APIs, OpenAPI/GraphQL schemas, request validation, route handlers, auth middleware, or database migrations that shape the frontend contract. | Building UI components, client-side state, styling, or accessibility — delegate to The Frontend Engineer. Auth threat modeling, rate-limiting policy, and security audits go to The Web Security Auditor; smoke/integration test authoring goes to The Web QA Engineer. |
| fe | `web-fe` | standard | Building or modifying UI components, styling, accessibility (ARIA/axe), client-side routing, Storybook stories, or data-bound views against an API contract | Backend services, API contract design (route to The API Designer), structural/architectural decisions (route to The Web Architect), or cross-browser QA verification (route to The Web QA Engineer) |
| webarch | `web-webarch` | deep-think | Delegate for framework selection/upgrades, rendering-strategy decisions (SSR/SSG/ISR/CSR), monorepo package boundaries, cache-control and CDN topology, design-system governance, or any cross-cutting architectural trade-off requiring an RFC/ADR. | Do NOT take feature-level component implementation (route to The Frontend Engineer), API contract design (route to The API Designer), test authoring (route to The Web QA Engineer), or vulnerability remediation (route to The Web Security Auditor). |
| webqa | `web-webqa` | fast | End-to-end/cross-browser test authoring or review, Playwright/Cypress suites, Lighthouse performance/accessibility budgets, visual-regression diffing, or filing/triaging bug reports for web features marked ready for QA. | Writing the feature UI or React components (route to The Frontend Engineer), designing or implementing APIs (route to The API Designer), or release/architecture sign-off decisions (route to The Web Architect). |
| websec | `web-websec` | think | Auditing web code, configs, or dependencies for vulnerabilities — OWASP Top 10 checks, security header/CSP validation, npm/pnpm dependency audits, secret scanning, auth/session/token review, or CORS policy enforcement before merge or release. | Building features or designing APIs/auth flows themselves (defer to The API Designer), or front-end UI/UX and architecture decisions (defer to The Web Architect); this member reviews and blocks risk, it does not author product code. |

### 🐹 go — Go Development

| member | invoke | tier | use when | avoid |
|--------|--------|------|----------|-------|
| goarch | `go-goarch` | deep-think | Designing or reviewing service boundaries, defining Go interfaces before implementation, governing .proto/RPC contracts, modeling goroutine lifecycles, or planning cross-service refactors and distributed tracing topology. | Routine feature implementation (delegate to The Go Developer), test authoring or QA gating (The Go QA Engineer), or dependency/security vulnerability work (The Go Security Engineer). |
| godev | `go-godev` | standard | Writing or modifying Go source — implementing services, CLIs (cobra), libraries, concurrency, error handling, or module hygiene in cmd/, internal/, or pkg/. | Test authoring or coverage validation (delegate to The Go QA Engineer); package or service boundary design (delegate to The Go Architect); dependency CVEs or security findings (delegate to The Go Security Engineer). |
| goqa | `go-goqa` | fast | Validating a Go implementation marked Ready for QA — running the race detector, writing fuzz/benchmark/integration tests, enforcing coverage gates, or chasing goroutine leaks and flaky tests. | Writing the production Go implementation itself (hand to The Go Developer), high-level system design (hand to The Go Architect), or dependency/supply-chain security (hand to the security team). |
| gosec | `go-gosec` | think | A Go change needs a security review: gosec/govulncheck findings, new go.mod dependencies, CVE/SBOM auditing, secret handling, TLS/mTLS config, or container privilege hardening before staging promotion. | General Go feature implementation or refactoring (route to The Go Developer), architectural redesign (route to The Go Architect), or test-coverage work (route to the Go QA member). Also skip non-Go security domains. |

### ☁️ terraform-aws — Terraform & AWS

| member | invoke | tier | use when | avoid |
|--------|--------|------|----------|-------|
| cloudarch | `terraform-aws-cloudarch` | deep-think | Designing AWS account topology, landing zones, VPC/network tiers, multi-region RPO/RTO strategy, ADRs, or evaluating designs against the Well-Architected pillars and cost governance. | Hands-on Terraform module implementation (delegate to The Infrastructure Engineer), security posture audits (The Cloud Security Engineer), or CI/CD pipeline setup (The Platform Engineer). |
| cloudsec | `terraform-aws-cloudsec` | think | Static policy scanning of Terraform (checkov/tfsec), IAM role and policy audits, encryption-at-rest enforcement, CloudTrail/VPC Flow Log verification, S3 public access blocks, or SCP guardrail authoring. | Authoring net-new infrastructure modules or resources (delegate to The Infrastructure Engineer); high-level architecture decisions (delegate to The Cloud Architect); CI/CD pipeline build mechanics (delegate to The Platform Engineer). |
| infra | `terraform-aws-infra` | standard | Authoring or refactoring Terraform modules, composing root modules in environments/, writing variable blocks, configuring remote state, reviewing terraform plan output, or applying tagging and lifecycle rules to AWS resources | High-level architecture decisions (delegate to The Cloud Architect), IAM/policy and security posture review (delegate to The Cloud Security Engineer), or CI/CD pipeline implementation (delegate to The Platform Engineer) |
| platform | `terraform-aws-platform` | fast | Setting up or fixing CI/CD pipelines, GitHub Actions workflows, Atlantis configs, ECR lifecycle policies, ECS/EKS rollouts, container build automation, or CI secret handling via OIDC for AWS workloads. | Authoring Terraform modules or core infrastructure (delegate to The Infrastructure Engineer); IAM policy design or security posture review (delegate to The Cloud Security Engineer). |

### 🤖 ai-ci — AI & CI

| member | invoke | tier | use when | avoid |
|--------|--------|------|----------|-------|
| aiarch | `ai-ci-aiarch` | deep-think | Designing or reviewing agentic workflows, RAG/retrieval architecture, multi-model chains, model tier policies, eval harnesses, or LLMOps system design and ADRs | Implementation of the designed systems (delegate to The AI Developer), production model serving/inference ops (delegate to The Model Ops Engineer), or wiring evals into pipelines (delegate to The CI Engineer) |
| aidev | `ai-ci-aidev` | standard | Building or modifying LLM-backed features — prompt pipelines, RAG, embeddings, structured-output parsing, model-abstraction wrappers, or eval suites under evals/ | CI pipeline wiring or GitHub Actions belongs to The CI Engineer; model serving/inference infrastructure belongs to The Model Ops Engineer; novel retrieval/agentic architecture decisions belong to The AI Architect |
| ci | `ai-ci-ci` | fast | Authoring or fixing CI pipelines — GitHub Actions YAML, Makefile targets, caching strategy, build matrices, runner provisioning, concurrency controls, or speeding up lint/test jobs. | Writing the application/test code itself (delegate to The AI Developer) or GPU/model evaluation infrastructure (delegate to The Model Ops Engineer). |
| modelops | `ai-ci-modelops` | fast | The session needs to deploy, configure, or scale model-serving stacks (Ollama/LiteLLM/vLLM), manage GPU resource limits and VRAM, maintain the model registry, set inference latency SLOs, or design canary rollouts and air-gap model mirrors. | Authoring application or AI agent code (route to The AI Developer), building CI pipelines and smoke-test automation (route to The CI Engineer), or broad infrastructure redesign and capacity architecture (route to The AI Architect). |

### 🏛️ architecture — Architecture

| member | invoke | tier | use when | avoid |
|--------|--------|------|----------|-------|
| em | `architecture-em` | deep-think | The main session needs cross-team conflict resolution among architects, translation of business goals into engineering objectives, roadmap or risk-register updates, priority arbitration, or plain-language stakeholder summaries of architectural decisions. | Hands-on system design (delegate to the systems architect), deep implementation or code-level work (delegate to the principal engineer), security threat modeling (delegate to the security architect), or QA test strategy (delegate to the quality team). |
| principal | `architecture-principal` | deep-think | A change touches auth, data migrations, public APIs, or core infrastructure and needs a mandatory critical review; engineering standards, linter configs, or the design pattern library must be defined or enforced; tech debt must be cataloged or prioritized for sprint allocation. | High-level system structure, service boundaries, or topology decisions belong to The Systems Architect; team process, staffing, and persistent-violation escalation belong to The Engineering Manager; feature implementation belongs to the delivery teams. |
| secarch | `architecture-secarch` | deep-think | Designing or reviewing security architecture — STRIDE threat models, zero-trust enforcement, identity/OAuth2/OIDC flows, secrets management strategy, compliance mapping (SOC 2, GDPR, HIPAA), or blast-radius analysis of a new service or major feature. | Implementing application features, runtime incident response, or systems-level design without a security angle — route general architecture to The Systems Architect, prioritization/sequencing to The Engineering Manager, and domain implementation to the cloud/go/web engineers. |
| sysarch | `architecture-sysarch` | deep-think | Significant design decisions, service-boundary or data-store choices, multi-team/multi-service changes, cross-cutting contracts (observability/auth/error propagation), dependency-graph review, or capacity modeling before production. | Single-domain implementation details — defer web/Go/cloud/AI build work to the respective domain architects, test design to the QA team, and dependency/security hardening to the security team. Escalate cross-team conflict resolution to The Engineering Manager. |

## Squads (cross-team)

| squad | members | when |
|-------|---------|------|
| `fullstack-feature` | web/fe, web/api, go/godev, architecture/sysarch | Build a user-facing feature end to end (UI + API + service + design). |
| `secure-release` | go/gosec, web/websec, architecture/secarch | Security gate before shipping (code, web surface, threat model). |
| `infra-rollout` | terraform-aws/infra, terraform-aws/platform, terraform-aws/cloudsec | Provision and ship infrastructure changes safely. |
